subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of energy?
questions.explain: Energy, in all its forms, is measured in joules (J).

questions.q: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.explain: Power is the rate of energy transfer and is measured in watts, where 1 W = 1 J/s.

questions.q: Which equation correctly gives the work done by a force?
options: work done = force x distance moved
questions.explain: Work done equals the force multiplied by the distance moved in the direction of the force.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the principle of conservation of energy?
options: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only changed from one form to another
Energy is always lost when it is transferred
Energy can be created but never destroyed
Energy can be destroyed but never created
questions.explain: The Principle of Conservation of Energy: energy can be changed from one form to another but the total amount of energy does not change.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy resource?
questions.explain: Wind is renewable because it will not run out on a human timescale, unlike fossil fuels.

questions.q: Which of these is a non-renewable energy resource?
questions.explain: Coal is a fossil fuel that forms over millions of years and is used up faster than it is replaced.

questions.q: Which equation gives power in terms of work done?
questions.explain: Power is the work done (energy transferred) divided by the time taken.

questions.q: A moving car has energy because of its motion. Which form of energy is this?
questions.explain: Any moving object has kinetic energy because of its motion.

questions.q: Which equation correctly defines efficiency?
options: efficiency = useful energy output ÷ total energy input
efficiency = total energy input ÷ useful energy output
efficiency = useful energy output x total energy input
efficiency = wasted energy ÷ total energy input
questions.explain: Efficiency compares the useful energy transferred with the total energy supplied, often shown as a percentage.

questions.q: When energy is wasted (dissipated), in which form is it usually transferred to the surroundings?
questions.explain: Wasted energy is normally transferred to the surroundings as heat, warming them slightly.

questions.q: As a book is lifted slowly onto a higher shelf, which form of energy increases?
questions.explain: Raising an object higher above the ground increases its gravitational potential energy.

questions.q: As a ball falls freely towards the ground, which energy transfer takes place?
options: Gravitational potential energy to kinetic energy
Kinetic energy to gravitational potential energy
questions.explain: As the ball falls it loses height and speeds up, so its gravitational potential energy is changed into kinetic energy.

questions.q: Why can no real machine ever be 100% efficient?
options: Some energy is always dissipated to the surroundings, often by heating due to friction
Machines create extra energy that is lost
The total energy input is always destroyed
Useful energy output is always greater than the input
questions.explain: Friction and other effects always waste some energy as heat, so useful output is less than total input.

questions.q: Electrical energy is being transferred when...
options: a charge moves through a circuit
an object is heated by a flame
a force pushes an object along
questions.explain: Electrical energy is transferred when charge is moved through a circuit by an electric current.

questions.q: Motor A is more powerful than Motor B. This means Motor A...
options: transfers energy at a faster rate
transfers a smaller total amount of energy
can never do any useful work
questions.explain: A higher power means a greater rate of energy transfer, i.e. more joules transferred each second.

questions.q: Which is a major environmental disadvantage of burning fossil fuels?
options: They release carbon dioxide, contributing to climate change
They release no gases at all
They produce radioactive waste as their main product
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas linked to global warming and climate change.

questions.q: A force of 20 N moves a box 5 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
questions.explain: Work done = force x distance = 20 N x 5 m = 100 J.

questions.q: A 2 kg ball moves at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy? (Ek = ½ x mass x speed²)
questions.explain: Kinetic energy = ½ x 2 x 3² = ½ x 2 x 9 = 9 J.

questions.q: A 5 kg mass is lifted 2 m. Using g = 10 N/kg, how much gravitational potential energy does it gain? (Ep = mass x g x height)
questions.explain: Ep = mgh = 5 kg x 10 N/kg x 2 m = 100 J.

questions.q: A device is supplied with 200 J of energy and transfers 150 J usefully. What is its efficiency?
questions.explain: Efficiency = useful output ÷ total input = 150 ÷ 200 = 0.75 = 75%.
